exposure: clinical manifestations (apnea, respiratory distress, hypoxia, poor feeding)
cohort: The study included 88 neonates diagnosed with early neonatal sepsis who had procalcitonin levels greater than 2 ng/ml at 24 hours of life.
finding: Median procalcitonin concentrations at 24 hours were 15.1 ng/ml, and apnea, poor nutrition, and hypoxia were identified as the best predictors for early neonatal sepsis.
